items.title: The daily outward sweep — bring back work this site could not have thought of by looking at itself

items.detail:
Both pages state in their own voice that the old slug "still answers and still serves" (4.8) / "the slug still answers, and existing requests still serve" (5). The sourcing is sound — OpenRouter's notice says exactly that, and it is quoted and cited — but the router's own endpoints API disagrees in shape: GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/anthropic/claude-opus-4.8-fast/endpoints returns HTTP 200 with the model record and an empty "endpoints" array (same for claude-opus-5-fast and claude-opus-4.7-fast; the surviving standard rows return 8, 11 and 10 endpoints respectively). Measured 2026-09-02. Nothing published resolves whether an empty endpoints list means the slug is aliased internally or genuinely unroutable, and it cannot be settled without an API key. A clause of the form "the model record still answers, though the router's endpoints listing for it is now empty; OpenRouter's notice is the authority that requests still route" would keep the reader's trust if they run the same check.

items.detail:
The summary field still reads "with GLM-5.3 state of the art on CyberGym and ExploitGym". The card's own table, which this diff just read, puts GLM-5.3 third on the ExploitGym row — 105 / 130, behind Fable 5's 181 / 247 and the bolded GPT-5.6 Sol at 216 / 293. The card's prose does not make that claim either: it says "GLM-5.3 is state of the art on CyberGym for vulnerability discovery, and its gains are largest further up the exploitation chain, where it more than doubles GLM-5.2 on exploitation benchmarks" — SOTA is asserted for CyberGym only, and the exploitation sentence is a comparison against GLM-5.2, not a field-wide claim. Fix: narrow the summary to "state of the art on CyberGym", and if the ExploitGym gain is worth keeping, state it as the card does (more than triples GLM-5.2 at both budgets) rather than as a superlative. This matters because the post job draws its framing from this summary.

items.detail:
The new evidence text calls the two values "the 2-hour timeout budget" and "the 6-hour", which reads as wall-clock. The card's footnote says the budgets are "calculated as the API inference time rescaled by per-model tokens per second rate (per-model TPS sourced from Artificial Analysis; that is, we rescale GLM-5.3's results by 115 TPS, Kimi K3's results by 40 TPS and Qwen3.8 Max's results by 47 TPS), plus the non-API overhead." A 115-vs-40 TPS rescaling is exactly the methodology point a skeptical reader raises about a cross-model exploitation comparison. Fix: add the rescaling to the evidence line's footnote parenthetical so the post inherits it rather than having to rediscover it.
